headline: Ocean Ghost Nets Find New Life as Car Floor Mats
meta_description: Hyundai and Healthy Seas recover abandoned fishing nets from the ocean and transform them into floor mats for new cars, removing marine debris while creating s…
summary_short: Divers off Catalina Island are recovering abandoned fishing nets—ghost nets that trap marine life—and Hyundai is recycling them into car floor mats.
body:
A partnership between Hyundai and the nonprofit Healthy Seas is turning ocean waste into automotive innovation. Divers working off Catalina Island recovered tangled ghost nets from the sunken wreck of the fishing vessel Midnight Hour, which has sat on the ocean floor for 15 years, trapping debris and endangering marine life. Rather than remaining refuse, the recovered netting is being processed and separated—with suitable nylon material regenerated into recycled yarn called ECONYL, which is then manufactured into floor mats for Hyundai vehicles like the IONIQ, INSTER, SANTA FE, and NEXO sold in Europe.

Since 2013, Healthy Seas has recovered more than 1,300 tons of nets and marine debris worldwide. Hyundai joined the mission in 2021, and the partnership has now expanded to ten countries, recovering more than 320 tons of marine litter. The work near Catalina is part of a larger initiative called From Sea to Shore, which combines ocean recovery with community engagement—including beach cleanups with Hyundai employees at Huntington State Beach and educational workshops for children at local Boys & Girls Clubs.

What makes this effort remarkable is its completeness. Divers physically remove the hazard to wildlife, the recovered material avoids landfills through recycling, and the process closes a loop by creating useful products. As Veronika Mikos, Director of Healthy Seas, noted, the mission connects "removing litter from the coast, recovering ghost fishing gear from the ocean, and inspiring children to understand and protect marine life." It's a reminder that yesterday's ocean debris can become tomorrow's responsible manufacturing—if the right partnerships exist to make it happen.
quick_facts: Hyundai and Healthy Seas partner to recycle ocean ghost nets into car floor mats
1,300+ tons of nets recovered globally since 2013
Divers worked off Catalina Island to recover nets from 15-year-old shipwreck
320 tons of marine litter recovered across ten partner countries
Recycled nylon (ECONYL) used in IONIQ, SANTA FE, and other Hyundai models
